consistency_checks.detail: All severity ≥3 findings are linked to at least one diagnosis

top_concerns: Missing family history and physical signs for FH
Absence of BMI, waist circumference, triglycerides, and HDL‑C to confirm metabolic syndrome
No thyroid function tests to evaluate hypothyroidism
Lack of aldosterone/renin measurements for primary aldosteronism
Iron studies and complete anemia work‑up are absent
review_summary: The differential captures the major high‑severity abnormalities and includes appropriate secondary considerations. Probability weighting has been refined, especially raising the likelihood of a primary lipid disorder and CKD while keeping metabolic syndrome as the leading diagnosis. Key data gaps (family history, BMI, triglycerides, thyroid and aldosterone panels, iron studies, medication list) must be addressed to move diagnoses from plausible to confirmed.
